normalized.governing_thought: Harlow can return to a 3.0% margin by FY2028 by reversing what caused the decline, not by cutting store hours
executive_summary: The problem: Operating margin fell from 3.4% to 1.0% in two years. Operating income fell from $47.9M to $15.3M while sales grew 6%.

The cause: Heavier promotions (−0.70 pts), e-commerce fulfillment (−0.84) and higher shrink (−0.50) explain 2.0 of the 2.4-point fall. Store labor explains 0.3: wages rose 9.4%, but hours per $ of sales fell 6%.
The draft plan falls short: Cutting store hours 8% saves $14.5M on paper, but the stores with the fewest hours already have the most shrink. The draft plan reaches 1.1–1.8% in FY2028, not 3.0%.

Recommendation: Five moves worth ~$30M a year by FY2028: reset promotions, rebalance labor to cut shrink, price delivery closer to cost, exit the 9 loss-making stores, grow private label. After the 2027 wage rise, operating income reaches ~$42M, a 3.0% margin.

Act first: In the next 90 days: roll out the tested delivery fee, drop loss-making promotions, replace the hours cut with a rebalance, hold the delivery contract rate, give notice on 6 expiring leases. FY2026 operating income: ~$24M against the $20M covenant.
The risk: 3.0% needs every move to deliver. The moves within management's control reach ~2.3%. The rest depends on vendor talks, a second delivery-price test and a board vote on 3 stores.

slides.title: Choices we made where the briefing pack is silent

claims.claim: Timing: The pack has actuals to FY2025 and treats FY2026 as the first plan year ... We do the same. If FY2026 (ending January 2027) has already closed when the board meets, replace the covenant outlook with the actual and discuss it with the lender. The FY2027–28 plan does not change.

Constant terms: The plan is sized at FY2025 prices and volumes, with no market growth. Routine cost inflation is assumed to be covered by price. The 2027 minimum-wage step is the only headwind we model explicitly.
Cannibalization: The 70% of online sales that would otherwise be made in-store are assumed to earn the same margin in either channel.
What we have not counted
evidence: One-time costs other than the $7.5M lease exits (closures, private-label development, shrink tools). Finance should cost these within the $17.5M left.
Any renegotiated cut in the delivery partner’s rate (each 5% ≈ $0.5M).
Theft, 35% of shrink, beyond what better receiving catches.
Further ValuMart openings, which would add to the pressure on traffic.

evidence: Whether the 14-pt promotional gap is measured after vendor funding.
Labor hours and sales by quartile, and by each of the 9 weak stores.
Lease-end dates for the 6 stores, which set when their savings start.

normalized.recommendation: Five moves worth ~$30M a year by FY2028: reset promotions, rebalance labor to cut shrink, price delivery closer to cost, exit the 9 loss-making stores, grow private label. After the 2027 wage rise, operating income reaches ~$42M, a 3.0% margin. Board asked to: endorse the five-move plan and its first-90-day actions, in place of the 8% hours cut and the e-commerce freeze; agree to vote in Q2 FY2027 on exiting 3 long-lease stores (up to $7.5M) if their four-wall EBITDA is still negative; accept a delivery service priced nearer its cost; authorize the CEO and CFO to brief the lender this month.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected. Saves $14.5M on paper, but the stores with the fewest hours already have the most shrink; up to −$9.4M shrink given back; reaches 1.1–1.8% in FY2028, not 3.0%; leaves promotions, delivery and shrink untouched. Replaced by a labor rebalance (trim most labor-intensive stores, put half back in the leanest).
Board asked to endorse the five-move plan in place of the 8% hours cut and the e-commerce freeze; delivery stays, priced nearer its cost.

alternatives_considered.treatment: To be tested in FY2027 in a few stores; scale in FY2028 if it pays (~+$2.5M, illustrative).

assumptions_and_uncertainties: 3.0% needs every move to deliver. The moves within management’s control reach ~2.3%. The rest depends on vendor talks, a second delivery-price test and a board vote on 3 stores.
The full plan has no buffer above 3.0% (full plan 3.04%).

Plan values are annual run-rates in constant FY2025 terms (FY2025 prices and volumes, no market growth); routine cost inflation assumed covered by price; 2027 minimum-wage step is the only headwind modelled explicitly.
Shrink-hours link (FY2023–25 pattern) is a correlation, not proof of cause.
Promotion cut assumes a third of the cut volume is lost and two-thirds sells at full price (our assumption).
Vendor funding sizing assumes the 14-pt gap is after vendor funding (inference: confirm with finance).
Deeper promotions coincided with weaker ValuMart-area sales; this does not prove cause.
Sales moved online from stores assumed to earn the same margin either way; the cannibalization survey (n = 2,300) is self-reported.
Store figures for the 6 and the 3 are split pro rata by store count, because store-level data are not in the pack; depreciation and allocated overhead are ignored.
Labor rebalance uses an assumed hours split (most labor-intensive quartile ≈28% of hours).
Second delivery step sizing is illustrative; to be tested.
Wage step assumes half offset by price and productivity (our assumption).
FY2026 headroom is thin; outlook assumes the FY2023–25 slide stops; if ValuMart keeps pulling sales down, headroom shrinks.
FY2026 outlook excludes one-time costs; one-time costs other than $7.5M lease exits not yet costed.
Not counted: renegotiated delivery partner rate cut (each 5% ≈ $0.5M), theft (35% of shrink) beyond what better receiving catches, further ValuMart openings.
If FY2026 has already closed when the board meets, replace the covenant outlook with the actual.
To validate: whether the 14-pt promotional gap is after vendor funding; labor hours and sales by quartile and by each of the 9 weak stores; lease-end dates for the 6 stores.
next_steps: In the next 90 days: roll out the tested delivery fee ($7.99, free from $100), drop loss-making promotions, replace the hours cut with a rebalance, hold the delivery contract rate, give notice on 6 expiring leases.

normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text, with no images. The charts appear only as loose labels and numbers, so I paired them by their order. That pairing is my best reading, especially for the shrink-by-quartile values on slide 4 and the bridge segments on slides 8 and 10. Slide 12's table text is interleaved with the decision numbers. Status colours are described only in the footnote.
